SMTO-RST-0001 — This task needs your decision about a blocked job first

GUID: e6a1a758-21ff-4a7a-a790-7b8493a95f22
Slug: legacy-continuation-required
Domain: RST · Subsystem: rst

What happened

  • This older task is paused because a job it depends on is still holding resources, and it needs your choice before it can go on. The command it was waiting to run hasn't started.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. Open the task's conversation and find the card marked A recovery decision is needed or Job recovery. That card is the only way this task accepts the decision it's waiting for.
  2. Read the card's blocking job status to check whether the earlier job has already finished or is still running. Check whether the earlier action already happened, so you don't stop work that is nearly done or run it twice.
  3. Select Wait until the job state changes to let the job finish, or Resolve forcefully by terminating job only if you're sure it should stop. Waiting lets the task continue on its own; terminating ends the job and frees what it was holding right away.

What success looks like

  • The card shows Job state updated or Blocking job claims restored, and the task continues.

If it still fails

  • Check whether the earlier action already happened before you try anything again. Select Copy error details and send them to the person who manages SMTO. Don't resend the same request in a new message while the old job's outcome is unclear; that could run the command twice.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • Resume found an older run in the awaiting_resource_reconciliation state but the request did not carry the required resource_reconciliation decision, so it was rejected with 409.

What this means

  • Resume finds the historical awaiting_resource_reconciliation state without its required resource_reconciliation control input. State diagnostics preserve authoritative journal, ownership and effect evidence. They do not delete records, loosen ownership fences, issue SQL or restart/replay work; missing persistence confirmation is separate from in-memory acceptance.

Why this can happen

  • Resume finds the historical awaiting_resource_reconciliation state without its required resource_reconciliation control input.

How to diagnose it

  • Inspect the original reconciliation state and supported historical controls instead of treating ordinary Resume as sufficient.

How to fix it

  • The run is in the historical awaiting_resource_reconciliation state; continue it only through the native resource-reconciliation route with the current decision_id and blocker_revision (the Job recovery card's Wait or Resolve forcefully actions), after inspecting the blocking job's current state. Do not resume it through ordinary Resume or repeat its mutation while the earlier outcome is unresolved.
  • Open the run’s historical baseline controls and reconcile recorded state before choosing its supported continuation.

Retry and execution caution

  • Inspect and reconcile authoritative state before repeating a mutation. Do not blindly retry.

How to verify the fix

  • The exact retained decision is resolved through its supported control flow.

What not to do

  • Do not repeat a mutation while the earlier outcome or current owner is unresolved.

Technical notes

  • State diagnostics preserve authoritative journal, ownership and effect evidence. They do not delete records, loosen ownership fences, issue SQL or restart/replay work; missing persistence confirmation is separate from in-memory acceptance.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.

Do not confuse with / related errors

  • SMTO-EXE-0004 — Execution outcome is unknown
